# Vessel First

The deliverable is the vessel. The content is the cargo.
Build the vessel before you have the cargo.

## The rule

Create the named place first. Empty is fine.

If the ask names a branch, a file, a record, a ticket — create it
on move one. The work goes into something that already exists.

## Why empty is enough

A named, empty vessel survives interruption.

A perfect cargo with no vessel does not exist to anyone but you.

## Iterate inside the vessel

Add a little. Land it. Add more. Land that.

Do not accumulate work outside the vessel and pour it in at the end.
The end may not arrive.

## WIP is delivery

A rough commit on the named branch beats a polished diff in your head.

Name commits "wip: <thing>" if they are unfinished. They still count
as the shape of the work being on the right surface.

## Squash later, never first

If the harness reads at any moment, what does it find?

If the answer is "nothing yet, I'm still preparing" you have the
order wrong. Land the rough thing. Refine in place.

## Closing

Before you stop, ask: does the named place exist, and does it
contain the latest version of the work? If not, that is the
last move, not summarising what you did.
